reason: The canonical corrected assertion is unbounded attainable regret for some reward best response when zero is feasible, positive-treatment nondegeneracy holds, and the expected reward is invariant under changes preserving the joint law of (X,Y1). All these hypotheses, the shifted law, invariance and optimizer preservation, welfare and regret formulas, explicit B=(M+1)/c, and zero-reward tie example are stated. The abstract reward(D,policy) represents the expected-reward functional and even allows additional functionals satisfying the same hypotheses. Real suprema agree with maxima on every constructed law because zero attains welfare 0.

The claim is specifically the failure of the printed agent-to-reference absolute-continuity condition alone to supply a reference-to-agent representing density. The statement gives the exact Lebesgue/half-atom measures, normalization, common support, domination, atom masses, failed reverse absolute continuity and density nonexistence, and completes both one-unit oracle agents with admissible unconstrained policies, independent seeds and constant nonnegative effects. The docstring expressly limits the refutation to this sufficiency reading. Using ambient R with support [0,1] instead of the Borel subtype [0,1] does not change the witness.

The statement includes the qualified canonical claim's corrected direction P0<<Pk, normalized RN weight, common baseline, reference-effect integrability, treated conditional unbiasedness and treated-residual/individual weighted-summand integrability for every policy and unit. It states (i)-(v), including attainment by the positive-effect policy, uniform ordering without nonnegative effects, and relative ordering when every effect is nonnegative. Each score uses its own experiment and each summand its own covariate. It correctly requires neither strict weight positivity nor untreated estimator integrability. The formulation also applies beyond common topological support and needs no cross-agent coupling, which are harmless extensions of the asserted marginal score identities and rankings.

The canonical statement explicitly identifies the formal content of this correction as pointwise positive-part monotonicity integrated against P0, with the separate score identities assigned to T30, T7 and T13. The theorem states positivePart=max(t,0), the full nonnegative extended-integral comparison, and its ordinary real-integral form when the quantities are integrable. Its extension to arbitrary measures and even lower integrals of nonmeasurable functions includes all the claim's ordinary measurable expectations; infinity is represented meaningfully rather than discarded by toReal.

Both canonical examples have their complete observed mass functions equated while untreated outcomes differ, all treatment probabilities are positive, the required covariate stratum has zero untreated probability, and the second has marginal untreated mass 1/4 with the three exact record probabilities. The universal singleton-private-coordinate clause proves maximum heterogeneity and its expectation are zero for both models. The claim refutes untreated identification and the inference that positive treatment supplies the untreated conditioning mass; neither theorem nor docstring asserts failure of a regret bound with an already well-defined estimator.
